subject: riotInterceptor
pitch:
Category: Vehicle.
Subject: corporate riot-control interceptor with a water cannon and neon light bars.
Style: Cyberpunk 2077.
reasoning:
I'm planning a single efficient TS module for a static armored riot truck model, around 5.6m long with a lower hull box, sloped-windshield cabin wedge, roof light, and large wheels, built from simple parts without any rigging.

I'll add roof water cannon turret, rear tank with logo, front ram plow, hazard stripes, glowing lights and neon underglow, plus an antenna and corp branding, using box and cylinder helpers for geometry with rotation set per axis. I'm working out exact dimensions now -- wheel radius and spacing, hull width and height, and where the hood and cab sections begin along the z-axis.

Mapping cabin, windshield, rear riot compartment, and roof light bar positions, then placing the turret base and barrel so it points forward over the cab roof.

I'm now adding neon underglow and side strips, glowing headlight and taillight boxes, a hazard-striped ram bumper, tinted windows, and a hexagonal emblem decal on the doors for corporate branding.

Still adding details: rear water tank cylinders with glowing gauges, armor plates, chevron rear doors, antenna, spotlight, and torus-ring neon wheel hubs. I'll write a small helper function to place geometry with color, position, and extra options.

Working out wheel placement with mirrored left/right rows and rotated cylinders so the lowest wheel sits flush at ground level, then angling the windshield box backward around the X-axis so its top edge tilts toward the rear of the cabin.
